parts.text: Lee draws circles on rectangular pieces of paper. He drops grains of rice at random onto the pieces of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside each circle.

content.tex: Lee draws circles on rectangular pieces of paper. He drops grains of rice at random onto the pieces of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside each circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Lee draws a circle of radius 5 cm on a rectangular piece of paper measuring 40 cm by 20 cm. The probability, p , that a grain of rice lands inside the circle is p = area of circle area of paper .

content.tex: Lee draws a circle of radius 5cm on a rectangular piece of paper measuring 40cm by 20cm.
The probability, \(p\) , that a grain of rice lands inside the circle is
\(p = \frac{area of circle}{area of paper}\) .

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Show that p is approximately 0.098 for this piece of paper.

content.tex: Show that \(p\) is approximately 0.098 for this piece of paper.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Lee drops 10 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. The diagram shows the result. The relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle = number of grains of rice inside the circle total number of grains of rice dropped . Find the relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle. ...................................................

content.tex: Lee drops 10 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. The diagram shows the result.
The relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle number of grains of rice inside the circle \(=\) . total number of grains of rice dropped
Find the relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Lee drops 10 more grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. Show that the relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle is 0.15 .

content.tex: Lee drops 10 more grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper.
Show that the relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle is 0.15 .

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) The relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle gives an estimate for the probability, p . The area of the circle is π 25 × . Use area of circle area of paper = 0.15 to show that an estimate for π is 4.8 .

content.tex: The relative frequency that a grain of rice is inside the circle gives an estimate for the probability, \(p\) .
The area of the circle is \(25\times \pi\) .
Use \(\frac{area of circle}{area of paper} = 0.15\) to show that an estimate for \(\pi\) is 4.8 .

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Use the formula area of circle area of paper = relative frequency to estimate π using the combined results for all 20 grains of rice. π = ...................................................

content.tex: Use the formula
\(\frac{area of circle}{area of paper} =\) relative frequency
to estimate \(\pi\) using the combined results for all 20 grains of rice.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Lee draws a circle of radius 12 cm on a different piece of paper. The circle touches all four edges of the paper. Lee drops 50 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He removes the 50 grains of rice and drops another 50 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. The combined number of grains of rice inside the circle is 78. Use the formula area of circle area of paper = relative frequency to estimate π . π = ...................................................

content.tex: Lee draws a circle of radius 12cm on a different piece of paper. The circle touches all four edges of the paper.

Lee drops 50 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He removes the 50 grains of rice and drops another 50 grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. The combined number of grains of rice inside the circle is 78.
Use the formula \(\frac{area of circle}{area of paper} =\) relative frequency to estimate \(\pi\) .

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Lee draws a circle of radius r cm on a different piece of paper. The circle touches all four edges of the paper. Show that, for any value of r , estimate for π = k × relative frequency, where k is an integer. Find the value of k . k = ...................................................

content.tex: Lee draws a circle of radius \(r\) cm on a different piece of paper. The circle touches all four edges of the paper.
Show that, for any value of \(r\) ,
estimate for \(\pi = k \times\) relative frequency, where \(k\) is an integer.
Find the value of \(k\) .

parts.text: Lee draws a circle on a piece of paper in the shape of a regular hexagon of side length x cm. The circle touches all six edges of the paper. Lee drops grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside the circle and finds the relative frequency.

content.tex: Lee draws a circle on a piece of paper in the shape of a regular hexagon of side length \(x\) cm. The circle touches all six edges of the paper.
Lee drops grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside the circle and finds the relative frequency.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Find an estimate for the value of π when x = 30 and the relative frequency that the grain of rice is inside the circle is 0.905 . Use the formula area of circle area of paper = relative frequency . ...................................................

content.tex: Find an estimate for the value of \(\pi\) when \(x = 30\) and the relative frequency that the grain of rice is inside the circle is 0.905 .
Use the formula \(\frac{area of circle}{area of paper} =\) relative frequency .

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Show that, for any value of x , estimate for π = k × relative frequency, where k is an exact constant. Find the value of k . k = ...................................................

content.tex: Show that, for any value of \(x\) ,
estimate for \(\pi = k \times\) relative frequency, where \(k\) is an exact constant.

parts.text: Lee draws a circle on a piece of paper in the shape of a regular polygon with n sides. The circle touches all n edges of the paper. He drops grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside the circle and finds the relative frequency. Estimate for π = k × relative frequency Explain clearly why the constant k gives an approximation for π , as the value of n increases.

content.tex: Lee draws a circle on a piece of paper in the shape of a regular polygon with \(n\) sides. The circle touches all \(n\) edges of the paper. He drops grains of rice at random onto the piece of paper. He counts the number of grains of rice inside the circle and finds the relative frequency.
Estimate for \(\pi = k \times\) relative frequency
Explain clearly why the constant \(k\) gives an approximation for \(\pi\) , as the value of \(n\) increases.
